description: Papaya salad tricycle cart: the rear half of a bicycle carrying a glass-cased sheet-steel cabinet in line ahead of it on two spoked wheels, joined by two chassis rails a side from the head tube and bottom bracket along the box; a folded blue tarp on four chrome poles above the case

image.prompt:
Product photograph of one isolated object, shot from a HIGH THREE-QUARTER ANGLE: the camera is well above the object and tilted down about 30 degrees, so the top of the object is clearly visible along with its front and one side. Not a straight-on elevation.

The object: A bicycle with a sidecar, exactly like a motorcycle sidecar: an ordinary upright bicycle and a separate tall glass-topped stainless steel display cart on a single spoked wheel stand side by side, parallel, with a wide gap of open air between them, joined only by two thick horizontal steel bars that run sideways from the bicycle's rear frame to the cart's underframe. Seen from the rear three-quarter so the bicycle's rear wheel and the cart's wheel sit next to each other with the two connecting bars clearly visible in the gap. Folded blue tarp canopy on poles above the cart Materials: weathered stainless steel, sun-bleached blue tarp, greasy glass.

Form: build the object from a few simple, chunky, closed volumes. Prefer solid panels over lattice, mesh, grilles or perforated screens; keep any openings few, large and clearly separated. No thin spindly protrusions, no wires, no chains, no fringes, no lace, no fine filigree, no dense repeated slots or cut-outs. Keep the silhouette simple and readable from every side. Keep the object's SHAPE simple; richness must come from the surface finish, wear and materials rather than from intricate geometry. The object is still photoreal and highly detailed in its texture -- only its form is simple.

Framing: long-lens near-orthographic perspective, minimal foreshortening. The object is perfectly centred and occupies about 75% of the frame height, with clear empty margin on all four sides. The whole object is in frame; nothing is cropped.

Background: completely flat seamless neutral 50% grey (#808080). The object floats in empty space against an infinite seamless backdrop, photographed as a cut-out with nothing underneath it. There is no surface for it to rest on and nothing for it to cast a shadow onto. No floor, no ground plane, no horizon line, no cast shadow, no contact shadow, no reflection, no vignette, no gradient.

Lighting: flat even studio illumination from all sides, soft and shadowless, like a lightbox. No strong key light, no rim light, no coloured light, no specular blowout, no dramatic highlights. Colours must read as true albedo.

One object only, nothing else in frame. No people, no hands, no other props, no packaging, no text, no labels, no watermarks, no measurement annotations, no arrows, no borders, no drop shadow.

Photoreal, sharp focus edge to edge, clean and undamaged geometry, realistic materials and surface wear. Not stylised, not cartoon, not low-poly, not a 3D render preview, not a wireframe.

license.notice: Fully synthetic. No third-party scanned or scraped geometry.

review.critique: FINAL VERDICT. Overall visual fidelity 0.91. 3,836/4,000 triangles, 3/4 draw calls, 2/4 materials, 3/8 unique geometries, one 256 px canvas. Open bicycle: turntable with --allow-holes on the _holecc measurement (the openings in the frame, under the box and between spokes are real air).

featureReviews.evidence: Proxy band table: mean |delta w| 0.059, |delta d| 0.016. Case bands 6-7 within 0.015 of the reference (0.379/0.255 against 0.381/0.255); tarp band 0.492/0.283 against 0.508/0.243. Residuals: band 5 +0.27 is the 5-95 percentile catching the saddle and handlebar that the proxy trimmed; band 2 -0.11 is the open rear wheel sampled thinner than the proxy's disc.
featureReviews.notes: Declared size re-derived to 1.80 x 1.52 x 0.60 on the 20-inch-wheel anchor; layout settled as a front-box tricycle on the proxy's side and end views.

featureReviews.evidence: Five 0.34-opacity panes (four sides and the top) in a chrome angle frame with mid mullions and a tray, 0.26 m tall over a 0.75 m cabinet with chrome corner angles; four chrome poles proud of a folded tarp roll with rounded long edges, two fold slabs and rope ties, with air under the roll as the plate shows.
featureReviews.notes: The plate's finer creases and the papaya inside the case are not carried.

featureReviews.evidence: Coherent frame: head, top, down and seat tubes closing on the bottom bracket, paired stays to the rear hub, seat post and sprung-saddle ellipsoid, rack with stays, mudguard, cranks and pedals a half turn apart, chainring, cassette and two chain runs, stem to a swept bar with grips. Ladder chassis: upper rails clamped at the head tube with end caps 0.25 m behind it, lower rails from the bottom bracket, both pairs along the box sides to its front, cross members at the clamps and the front. Three open wheels of tyre and rim ring lathes, hub and 28 prism spokes, instanced, each a named pivot.
featureReviews.notes: Nothing steers; both rail pairs are clamped to the fixed frame, recorded in assumptions.

notes: Declared size re-derived 2026-08-27 on the second plate (nano-banana-2 seed 11) and its Meshy proxy. Layout is a FRONT-BOX TRICYCLE, not a sidecar: the proxy's side view puts the box in line ahead of the bicycle's head tube, its end view puts two cart wheels at z +-0.16 H with the bicycle's wheel on the centreline, and the two bars are chassis rails at 0.47 H (head-tube clamp) and 0.17 H (bottom-bracket clamp) running along the box sides. Scale anchor: the wheels are 0.34 H in the proxy and 300 of 882 plate px = 0.34 H, so a 20-inch (0.518 m) wheel gives H = 1.52 m; proxy w:h:d 1.215:1:0.389 gives 1.85 x 1.52 x 0.59, built 1.77 x 1.52 x 0.64 and declared 1.80 x 1.52 x 0.60 (the handlebar and cart tyres set the depth). The previous 1.85 x 1.95 x 0.90 was the sidecar reading of the first plate.
